name: Git-Dumper - Dump Exposed .git Directories
description: Extracts an exposed .git directory from a web server, reconstructing the full repository locally. Recovers source code, configuration files, and commit history - often revealing hardcoded credentials, API keys, internal URLs, and application logic. Common in dev/staging servers that deploy via git without proper .gitignore or web server rules to block .git access.
source: CWL MCRTA Lab - AWS Cloud Red Teaming

examples.label: Step 2 - Dump exposed .git from target web server
Step 3 - Review recovered source code
examples.command:
cd /tmp/gitdump
ls -la
git log --oneline
git diff HEAD~1

examples.label: Step 4 - Search for secrets in commit history

variations.label: Check if .git is exposed before dumping
variations.description: Returns 200 if .git/HEAD is accessible - confirms the .git directory is exposed before running a full dump.

variations.label: Manual .git recovery without git-dumper
variations.description: Alternative manual approach using wget to mirror the .git directory and reconstruct the working tree.

notes: After recovering source code, look for: (1) hardcoded credentials and API keys, (2) internal URLs and IP addresses, (3) SSRF/RCE vulnerabilities in the code logic, (4) database connection strings, (5) .env files or config files with secrets. Check all branches and the full commit history - secrets are often removed from HEAD but still visible in older commits.

recommended.note: Source code may reveal SSRF-vulnerable endpoints to exploit for cloud metadata theft.
Recovered .git may contain AWS credentials or S3 bucket references.

defense.why_it_works: Web servers that deploy directly from git repositories often leave the .git directory accessible. The .git directory contains the full repository history including all commits, branches, and file contents - even files that were deleted or had secrets removed in later commits.
defense.prerequisites: Target web server with exposed .git directory. git-dumper or wget installed.
defense.impact: T1213 Data from Information Repositories + T1552.001 Unsecured Credentials: Credentials in Files. Full source code recovery enables further exploitation through discovered vulnerabilities and leaked credentials.
defense.detection: Web server access logs showing sequential requests to .git/ paths (objects, refs, HEAD, config). High volume of 200 responses to .git/* URIs from a single source IP.
defense.artifacts: Web server access logs: GET /.git/HEAD, GET /.git/objects/*, GET /.git/refs/* | IDS/WAF: pattern matching on .git path access
defense.splunk_spl:
index=web sourcetype="access_combined" uri_path="*/.git/*" status=200
| stats count dc(uri_path) as unique_paths by src_ip, host
| where count > 20 AND unique_paths > 5
defense.sentinel_kql:
W3CIISLog
| where csUriStem contains "/.git/"
| where scStatus == 200
| summarize count(), dcount(csUriStem) by cIP, bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)
| where count_ > 20
defense.prevention: Block access to .git directories in web server config (nginx: location ~ /\.git { deny all; }). Use .gitignore properly. Deploy built artifacts instead of git repositories. Use WAF rules to block .git path access.
